input: Map out a 10-day road trip itinerary

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The starting point, ending point, and geographic region entirely determine which routes, destinations, and stops are relevant — without this, no planning can begin.
Whether this is a solo trip, a couple, a family with kids, or a group of friends changes accommodation choices, activity types, pacing, and budget considerations significantly.
The overall budget per day or total shapes every decision — from where to sleep (camping vs. hotels) to dining and paid attractions.
The time of year affects weather, road conditions, crowd levels, and which attractions are open or worth visiting.
Knowing whether the traveler prioritizes nature/outdoors, cities/culture, food, adventure activities, or history defines which stops to include and how long to spend at each.
Whether the trip is a loop back to the start or a one-way point-to-point journey fundamentally changes the route structure and any transportation logistics at the end.
Understanding the desired pace — how many hours of driving per day, how many stops, how much free vs. structured time — defines what a 'good' itinerary looks like for this person.

gold.taskTitle: Map out a 10-day road trip itinerary
gold.taskDescription: Plan a detailed 10-day road trip itinerary covering routes, stops, and activities.

questions.title: Where does the trip start and end?
questions.description: Identify the departure city or region and whether the trip ends at the same place or a different destination.

questions.title: Who is traveling on this trip?
questions.description: Clarify the group composition — solo, couple, family with children, or friends — to tailor activities and accommodations.

questions.title: What is the total or daily budget?
questions.description: Establish a spending range to guide choices around lodging, dining, and paid activities.

questions.title: What time of year is the trip planned for?
questions.description: Determine the season or specific month to account for weather, road conditions, and seasonal availability of attractions.

questions.title: What type of experiences matter most to you?
questions.description: Identify the traveler's priorities — nature, cities, food, history, adventure — to curate the most relevant stops and activities.

questions.title: Is this a loop or a one-way point-to-point route?
questions.description: Clarify whether the trip returns to the starting point or ends at a different location, which shapes the entire route structure.

questions.title: How many driving hours per day feels comfortable?
questions.description: Understand the preferred pace — light driving with long stops vs. covering more ground — to structure each day realistically.
